title: Chicken & potatoes
description: A simple chicken-and-potato meal-prep base. The portion guide below comes from my saved five-container batch; adjust your own meal to what you need.
imageAlt: Seasoned sliced chicken and potatoes on a plate in James's kitchen.
caption: Chicken and potatoes from my kitchen. The pictured plate is a different serving from the portion guide below.
ingredients: 1,000 g cooked chicken breast (200 g per container)
300 g baked potato slices (60 g per container)
Cooking spray, as needed
Salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika, to taste
steps: Season the chicken with salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika. Cook until the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C), checked with a food thermometer. Rest, then slice or dice.
Slice the potatoes evenly, lightly coat with cooking spray and season. Bake at 425°F until browned and tender, flipping once. The time will depend on slice thickness and your oven.
Weigh the chicken and potatoes after cooking. Divide 1,000 g cooked chicken and 300 g baked potatoes among five containers: 200 g chicken and 60 g potatoes in each.
Cool and refrigerate promptly in shallow containers. Follow the storage guidance below; freeze portions you won't eat within the refrigerated window.
note: The quantities above describe the finished food. Cooking changes the weight, so don't use 1,000 g of raw chicken as a substitute for 1,000 g cooked. This is my recorded portion split, not a nutrition target for everyone.
nutritionNote: Nutrition will vary with the chicken, cooking fat, seasonings and portions. No unverified macro totals are included here.

title: Smoky chipotle beef pasta
description: Beef, penne and kidney beans with mozzarella and chipotle in adobo. This five-portion recipe comes from my meal-prep notebook.
ingredients: 2 lb lean ground beef
270 g dry Barilla Protein+ penne
430 g kidney beans, drained and rinsed
220 g reduced-fat mozzarella
200 g Rao's pizza sauce
50 g chipotle peppers in adobo, chopped
Salt, pepper, garlic powder and onion powder, to taste
steps: Cook the penne according to its package instructions until just tender, then drain.
Cook the ground beef over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks. Check that it reaches 160°F (71°C) with a food thermometer. Drain excess fat if needed and season to taste.
Stir in the drained kidney beans, pizza sauce and chopped chipotle peppers. Simmer for 3–5 minutes.
Fold in the pasta and mozzarella until evenly combined and the cheese has melted.
Divide into five portions. Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers and use the storage guidance below.
note: These are the brands and amounts recorded in my notebook. Changing the beef, pasta or cheese changes the nutrition. Add the ingredients you actually use to your own food log if you track.
nutritionNote: Contains wheat and dairy in the listed pasta and cheese; check your exact labels for other allergens. Nutrition totals are being left out until the labels and finished yield are checked.

title: Cheesy jalapeño ranch chicken burritos
description: Chipotle chicken, cheesy jalapeño ranch sauce and a tortilla toasted in a skillet. Makes six burritos.
imageAlt: Cheesy jalapeño ranch sauce in a pan beside a burrito toasting in a skillet.
caption: The sauce and a burrito in the skillet.
ingredients: 8 oz Philadelphia 1/3 Less Fat Cream Cheese
7 oz Great Value Reduced Fat Fiesta Blend Shredded Cheese
1 packet Hidden Valley Ranch Dip Mix (1 oz)
1 can La Victoria Mild Diced Green Chiles (can size not specified)
1 can Great Value Hot Diced Jalapeño Peppers (can size not specified)
A small splash of water, if needed
2 lb Costco Chargrilled Chipotle Chicken (about 151 g per burrito)
6 Don Pancho Carb Control Tortillas
Up to 600 g of the prepared sauce (100 g per burrito, if the batch makes enough)
steps: Warm the cream cheese in a saucepan over low to medium-low heat, stirring until softened. Add the shredded cheese gradually and stir until melted.
Mix in the ranch dip mix, green chiles and diced jalapeños. Stir until combined and creamy; add a little water if the sauce needs thinning.
Heat the chargrilled chipotle chicken according to its package directions. Divide the 2 lb package into six portions, about 151 g each.
Weigh the finished sauce. If it makes at least 600 g, use 100 g per burrito. If it makes less, divide what you have evenly rather than assuming the full amount.
Place one tortilla flat, add one portion of chicken and sauce, fold in the sides and roll tightly. Repeat for all six burritos.

If you like, toast the burritos in a skillet until golden on both sides. Cool and wrap individually or place in airtight containers before refrigerating or freezing. Reheat following the guidance below.
note: The supplied recipe calls for 600 g of prepared sauce, split six ways. It does not give the can sizes or a measured sauce yield, so weigh the finished batch before portioning.
nutritionNote: The supplied nutrition estimates are not included because the can sizes, exact product labels and finished sauce yield have not been verified. Check your ingredient labels for allergens; the listed sauce contains dairy.

title: BBQ jalapeño chicken
description: Chicken in a creamy BBQ sauce with onion, jalapeño and a little smoked paprika.
byline: From the Five Creamy Chicken Recipes collection
imageAlt: Chicken pieces cooking in a wire grilling basket over a smoky outdoor grill.
caption: Stock photo of grilled chicken, not this creamy skillet dish. Bulat Khamitov / Pexels.
ingredients: 1½ lb (680 g) raw boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tsp (9 g) olive oil, divided
½ cup (80 g) finely diced yellow onion
2 medium jalapeños (30 g), finely diced; remove seeds and ribs for less heat
1 tsp smoked paprika
½ tsp garlic powder
¼ tsp black pepper; salt to taste after adding sauce
½ cup (120 ml) low-sodium chicken broth
½ cup (120 g) sugar-free BBQ sauce
6 oz (170 g) fat-free cream cheese, softened and cubed
¾ cup (84 g) reduced-fat shredded fiesta/Mexican-blend cheese
steps: Pat the chicken dry; do not rinse it. Toss with smoked paprika, garlic powder and black pepper. Keep raw-chicken utensils separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.

Heat 1 tsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Brown half the chicken for 4–6 minutes, turning occasionally; transfer to a plate for partially cooked chicken. Repeat with remaining oil and chicken. It will finish cooking in the sauce.
Reduce to medium heat. Add onion and jalapeños and cook 3–4 minutes. Add a splash of the measured broth if they stick.
Add the remaining broth and BBQ sauce, scraping up browned bits. Lower the heat and whisk in cream cheese a few cubes at a time until smooth, about 2–3 minutes. Do not boil hard.

Return chicken and any juices to the pan. Cook gently 3–5 minutes, checking the thickest pieces for 165°F (74°C). Turn off heat and stir in shredded cheese until melted. Taste before adding salt; thin with water, 1 tbsp at a time, if needed.
Divide the chicken and all the sauce evenly into four servings.
note: This is a developed recipe idea, not a dish James has tested. One seeded jalapeño makes a milder version; leaving some ribs adds heat. Rice, broccoli or a baked potato are optional sides, not part of the four servings. Refrigerate leftovers 3–4 days and reheat to 165°F; the dairy sauce may turn grainy after freezing.
nutritionNote: Developed in the supplied Five Creamy Chicken Recipes collection. Not physically cooked or taste-tested. Nutrition estimates from that document are not published because they rely on representative ingredients rather than verified package labels. All four servings include the chicken and sauce; sides are separate. Contains dairy; check all packaged ingredients for other allergens.

title: Cajun cream chicken
description: Chicken, bell pepper and onion in a creamy Cajun-inspired skillet sauce.
byline: From the Five Creamy Chicken Recipes collection
imageAlt: A bowl of white pepper sauce with chicken pieces and dark pepper specks.
caption: Stock photo of chicken in white pepper sauce, not this Cajun recipe. dhiraj jain / Pexels.
ingredients: 1½ lb (680 g) raw boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tsp (9 g) olive oil, divided
2 tsp (about 6 g) Cajun seasoning, divided; choose a low-salt blend
½ cup (80 g) finely diced yellow onion
1 large bell pepper (150 g), diced
3 garlic cloves (9 g), minced
¾ cup (180 ml) low-sodium chicken broth
6 oz (170 g) fat-free cream cheese, softened and cubed
¾ cup (84 g) reduced-fat shredded cheddar
1 tbsp (15 ml) hot sauce, or less to taste
¼ tsp black pepper; salt only if needed at the end
steps: Pat chicken dry. Toss with 1 tsp Cajun seasoning and black pepper; reserve the second teaspoon for the sauce.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Brown half the chicken for 4–6 minutes, turning; move to a plate for partially cooked chicken. Repeat with remaining oil and chicken.
Reduce to medium heat. Cook onion and bell pepper 4–5 minutes, adding a splash of the measured broth if they stick. Add garlic and remaining Cajun seasoning and cook 30 seconds.
Add the remaining broth, scraping the pan. Lower heat. Whisk in softened cream cheese gradually until smooth, about 2–3 minutes. Stir in hot sauce; avoid a hard boil.
Return chicken and juices to the pan. Cook gently 3–5 minutes, checking several large pieces for 165°F (74°C). Remove from heat and stir in cheddar until melted. Taste before adding salt.
Divide chicken, vegetables and all sauce into four servings. Add water by the tablespoon if the sauce is too thick.
note: This is a developed recipe idea, not a dish James has tested. This is Cajun-inspired, not a traditional preparation. For less heat, use 1 tsp Cajun seasoning total and omit hot sauce. Rice or green beans are optional. Refrigerate leftovers 3–4 days and reheat to 165°F.
nutritionNote: Developed in the supplied Five Creamy Chicken Recipes collection. Not physically cooked or taste-tested. Nutrition estimates from that document are not published because they rely on representative ingredients rather than verified package labels. All four servings include the chicken and sauce; sides are separate. Contains dairy; check all packaged ingredients for other allergens.

title: Creamy salsa verde chicken
description: A chicken skillet with salsa verde, mild green chiles, lime and a creamy cheese sauce.
byline: From the Five Creamy Chicken Recipes collection
imageAlt: Green salsa being prepared in a stone mortar beside whole green tomatoes.
caption: Stock photo of green salsa preparation, not the finished chicken dish. Los Muertos Crew / Pexels.
ingredients: 1½ lb (680 g) raw boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tsp (9 g) olive oil, divided
1 tsp ground cumin
½ tsp garlic powder
¼ tsp black pepper; salt to taste after cooking
½ cup (80 g) finely diced yellow onion
1 cup (240 g) jarred salsa verde
1 (4 oz) can mild diced green chiles, drained (about 80 g solids)
¼ cup (60 ml) low-sodium chicken broth
6 oz (170 g) fat-free cream cheese, softened and cubed
¾ cup (84 g) reduced-fat shredded fiesta/Mexican-blend cheese
2 tbsp (30 ml) fresh lime juice, divided
¼ cup loosely packed chopped cilantro (8 g)
steps: Pat chicken dry and toss with cumin, garlic powder and black pepper. Save lime and cilantro for the end.

Heat 1 tsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Brown half the chicken for 4–6 minutes, turning; transfer to a plate for partially cooked chicken. Repeat with remaining oil and chicken.
Reduce heat to medium. Cook onion 3–4 minutes, using a splash of the measured broth if needed. Stir in salsa verde, drained chiles and remaining broth. Gently simmer 2 minutes.
Lower heat and whisk in softened cream cheese gradually until smooth. Avoid a hard boil to keep the dairy sauce from turning grainy.
Return chicken and juices to the pan. Cook gently 3–5 minutes, checking the largest pieces for 165°F (74°C). Remove from heat and stir in shredded cheese.
Stir in 1 tbsp lime juice and cilantro. Taste before adding the remaining lime or salt. Divide chicken and all sauce into four servings; thin with water by the tablespoon if needed.
note: This is a developed recipe idea, not a dish James has tested. Try mild salsa verde for less heat. Rice, cauliflower rice or warm tortillas are optional sides. Refrigerate leftovers 3–4 days and reheat to 165°F; dairy sauce may change texture after freezing.

title: Creamy pizza chicken
description: A chicken skillet with marinara, mozzarella, herbs and turkey pepperoni—pizza flavors, no crust.
byline: From the Five Creamy Chicken Recipes collection
imageAlt: Pepperoni pizza with tomatoes, olives and basil leaves.
caption: Stock photo of a pepperoni pizza, not the creamy chicken skillet. Shameel mukkath / Pexels.
ingredients: 1½ lb (680 g) raw boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tsp (9 g) olive oil, divided
¼ tsp black pepper; salt only if needed after cooking
3 garlic cloves (9 g), minced
1 tsp dried oregano
1 tsp dried basil
¼ tsp red pepper flakes, optional
1 cup (240 g) marinara sauce
¼ cup (60 ml) low-sodium chicken broth
6 oz (170 g) fat-free cream cheese, softened and cubed
1 cup (112 g) reduced-fat shredded mozzarella, divided
2 oz (56 g) turkey pepperoni, halved if large
steps: Pat chicken dry and season with black pepper. Measure mozzarella into ¾ cup for the sauce and ¼ cup for topping.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Brown half the chicken for 4–6 minutes, turning; move to a plate for partially cooked chicken. Repeat with remaining oil and chicken.

Reduce to medium-low. Cook garlic 30 seconds, adding a splash of the measured broth if the pan is dry. Add oregano, basil, optional pepper flakes, marinara and remaining broth. Simmer gently 2 minutes.
Lower heat and whisk in cream cheese in small additions until smooth, about 2–3 minutes. Stir in turkey pepperoni.
Return chicken and juices; cook gently 3–5 minutes, checking the largest pieces for 165°F (74°C). Turn off heat, stir in ¾ cup mozzarella and taste before adding salt.
Scatter the remaining ¼ cup mozzarella over the pan and cover off heat for 1–2 minutes to melt. Divide chicken, pepperoni and all sauce evenly into four servings.
note: This is a developed recipe idea, not a dish James has tested. The turkey pepperoni is part of the base recipe. Roasted zucchini, pasta or spaghetti squash are optional sides. Refrigerate leftovers 3–4 days and reheat to 165°F; mozzarella can become stringy when reheated.
nutritionNote: Developed in the supplied Five Creamy Chicken Recipes collection. Not physically cooked or taste-tested. title: Crispy chicken with creamy dill pickle sauce
description: Oven-baked panko chicken strips with a separate cheesy dill-pickle dipping sauce.
byline: From the Five Creamy Chicken Recipes collection
imageAlt: Breaded chicken tenders beside a small white cup of dipping sauce.
caption: Stock photo of fried chicken tenders and dip, not the baked pickle-sauce recipe. Valeria Boltneva / Pexels.
ingredients: 1½ lb (680 g) raw boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into ½-inch-thick strips
1 cup (60 g) plain panko breadcrumbs
1 tbsp (14 g) olive oil
1 large egg, beaten
1 tsp smoked paprika
½ tsp garlic powder
¼ tsp black pepper; up to ¼ tsp salt, optional
6 oz (170 g) fat-free cream cheese, softened and cubed
½ cup (120 ml) skim milk
½ cup (56 g) reduced-fat shredded cheddar
⅔ cup (100 g) finely chopped dill pickles, well drained
2 tbsp (30 ml) pickle brine, divided
2 tbsp (6 g) chopped fresh dill
½ tsp garlic powder
1 tsp hot sauce, optional
steps: Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a sheet pan with parchment rated for that temperature. Cut chicken into even ½-inch-thick strips and pat dry.
Mix panko with olive oil, smoked paprika, ½ tsp garlic powder, black pepper and optional salt. Put beaten egg in a second shallow bowl. Keep raw-chicken utensils separate from finished food.

Dip chicken into egg, let excess drip, then press into panko. Space strips in a single layer. Bake 18–22 minutes, turning halfway, until browned and the thickest strips reach 165°F (74°C). Check early; thickness matters. Discard leftover egg or coating that touched raw chicken.
While chicken bakes, warm milk and cream cheese in a small saucepan over low heat, whisking 3–5 minutes until smooth. Take off heat and stir in cheddar and the remaining ½ tsp garlic powder.
Stir in drained pickles, fresh dill, optional hot sauce and 1 tbsp pickle brine. Taste before adding the remaining brine. Thin with water by the tablespoon if needed.
Divide chicken and all sauce into four servings, keeping the sauce alongside for dipping rather than soaking the coating.
note: This is a developed recipe idea, not a dish James has tested. Keep cooked chicken and sauce separately in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. Reheat chicken in a 375°F oven and warm sauce gently, checking both for 165°F. Freezing may change sauce texture. Cabbage salad or roasted potatoes are optional sides.
nutritionNote: Nutrition estimates in the source are planning estimates from representative ingredient values, not verified labels. They count all measured egg and panko even if some coating is discarded. No macro totals are published here. Contains milk, egg and wheat; check packaged ingredients for additional allergens.
